review.tagline: Python framework for building LLM agents and apps from interoperable components
review.summary: LangChain is a Python library that gives a standard interface to chat models, embeddings, vector stores and tools, so providers can be swapped with little code change. Models load through init_chat_model with a provider:model string. For lower-level agent orchestration it points to LangGraph, and for tracing and evals to LangSmith.
review.audience: Python developers building LLM agents and applications in code
strengths: Common interface across model providers, embeddings and vector stores
Large integrations library covering tools, retrievers and vector stores
Companions: LangGraph for orchestration, Deep Agents for planning and subagents
MIT license; JS/TS counterpart available as LangChain.js
weaknesses: Observability, evals and managed deployment sit in LangSmith, a separate product
Controllable stateful agent workflows need LangGraph, not core LangChain
README gives no hardware requirements or list of supported providers
Abstraction layer is another API to learn on top of provider SDKs
needs: Needs Model provider API or other model backend
Models: OpenAI (README example), Other providers via integrations
